q: Does the Lemma-2 randomized LCU compilation of e^{i H t} actually deliver the promised L-independent per-sample gate scaling in practice, when composed with the Alg.-1 statistical loop, on a mid-sized (say 10-50 qubit, hundreds-of-terms) molecular Hamiltonian rather than only in the asymptotic Toffoli count?
basis: This replication substituted an exact statevector oracle for U_j, i.e., bypassed the paper's central algorithmic novelty. Confirming that the compiled U_j inside Alg. 1 preserves the shot-noise scaling (rather than injecting compilation bias that dominates at moderate delta) is unaddressed here.
next_steps: Implement Lemma 2 (random LCU with qDRIFT-style term sampling for U_j) using Qiskit or Cirq for a 6-8 qubit molecular H (e.g., H2, LiH in STO-3G) with L~15-30 Pauli terms. Sweep delta (compile precision) and measure whether std of tilde C(x_0) still follows N^{-1/2} at fixed compile cost, and whether the effective compile bias tracks the paper's O(delta) prediction. Free endpoint: run locally with numpy/scipy statevector; validate against a qiskit exact e^{iHt} reference.

q: How does the randomized SPE scheme compare head-to-head against modern shot-optimized ground-state estimators (classical shadows + energy estimation, adaptive Bayesian QPE, variational QPE) at fixed total shot budget on the same Hamiltonian?
basis: No comparison against Bayesian QPE (Wiebe-Granade 2016), robust phase estimation (Kimmel et al.), or shadow-based energy estimation (Huang-Kueng-Preskill 2020) was attempted. The paper's asymptotic Toffoli count vs. qDRIFT is quoted, but shot-count comparisons vs. these newer estimators are the more relevant NISQ-era benchmark.
next_steps: Set up a fixed problem (H2 or LiH in a small active space, exact eigenspectrum known). Implement three estimators in numpy statevector: (a) this paper's Alg.1, (b) Wiebe-Granade sequential Bayesian QPE, (c) grouped-Pauli shadow energy estimation. Sweep total shot budget from 10^3 to 10^6 and plot RMS energy error vs. shots for all three; report break-even points as a function of overlap eta. Free endpoints suffice (analytical + numpy).

q: Are the randomization schedules (F_j distribution + t_j grid) robust to realistic gate noise, and can noise-aware randomization schedules recover the shot-noise slope under depolarizing / T1-T2 channels at NISQ-era noise levels?
basis: Every simulation here was noiseless (statevector). The paper's error-suppression-by-sampling argument implicitly assumes coherent errors in U_j compilation; incoherent hardware noise on the Hadamard-test ancilla changes the story (bias in Re/Im estimator).
next_steps: Add a per-shot depolarizing / amplitude-damping channel to the Hadamard-test simulator (qiskit-aer noise model with p in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}). Measure whether N^{-1/2} slope survives and at what shot count noise-induced bias dominates variance. Then test whether reweighting F_j to prefer smaller |j| (shallower U_j) recovers precision at fixed physical shots. Free: qiskit-aer + local CPU.

q: For a specific target ground-state-energy problem where independent quantum-chemistry ground-truth exists (H2 at multiple bond lengths, LiH dissociation curve), does the Alg.-1 estimator recover the exact FCI curve to chemical accuracy within the paper's predicted shot budget?
basis: The reproduction here uses a 2-qubit TFIM, an abstract lattice Hamiltonian chosen for laptop tractability. The paper's motivating application is chemistry (FeMoco); no chemistry Hamiltonian was tested. Whether the constants (not just the scaling) yield chemical accuracy at plausible shot counts is unaddressed.
next_steps: Build an H2/STO-3G Hamiltonian via PySCF (free, local); compute FCI curve at 10 bond lengths as ground truth. Run Alg.1 with the exact-U_j statevector oracle at each point; report shot count needed for 1.6 mHa (chemical accuracy) at each bond length and compare against the paper's O(lambda^2/Delta^2 eta^2) prediction with real lambda, Delta, eta values from the Hamiltonian. Free: PySCF + numpy.

q: Can a hybrid adaptive protocol that interleaves this paper's randomized statistical estimator with an outer information-theoretic controller (Bayesian posterior over E_gs guiding the choice of the next t_j) beat the fixed-schedule Alg.1 in RMS-error-per-shot, and does that hybrid preserve the L-independence property?
basis: Alg.1 uses a fixed pre-sampled distribution over j. Modern Bayesian QPE (Wiebe-Granade, Ferrie-Granade-Cory) shows adaptive choice of query t and prior updates can reduce sample counts by 10-100x on the same underlying oracle. Whether the paper's L-independence argument survives an adaptive outer loop that concentrates queries near the estimated E_gs is open.
next_steps: Prototype an adaptive wrapper: maintain a Gaussian posterior over E_gs; at each step choose j to maximize expected information gain (equivalent to picking t_j that maximizes Fisher information at the current posterior mean); update posterior with the Hadamard-test Bernoulli outcome. Compare on the same TFIM as this report vs. Alg.1 fixed schedule at matched shot counts. Then argue analytically whether adaptive j-selection breaks the sum-over-|F_j| structure that underlies L-independence, or whether adaptivity acts only on the outer loop over x. Free: local numpy + scipy.stats.
